from typing import List, Tuple


def topo_order(n: int, deps: List[Tuple[int, int]]) -> Tuple[bool, List[int]]:
    """ Order the vertices 0 .. n-1 of a directed graph so that for every pair
    (a, b) in deps, a comes before b. Duplicate pairs are allowed.

    If such an order exists, return (True, order) where order is the
    lexicographically smallest valid order (at each step, the smallest vertex
    whose predecessors are all placed).

    If the graph has a cycle (a pair (a, a) is a cycle of one vertex), return
    (False, cycle): let s be the smallest vertex that lies on any cycle; cycle
    is the shortest cycle through s, written as its vertices starting at s
    without repeating s at the end; among shortest cycles, the
    lexicographically smallest list.

    Invalid input (n < 0, or any vertex in deps outside 0 .. n-1) returns
    (False, []), even if the graph also has a cycle. n == 0 gives (True, []).
    >>> topo_order(4, [(0, 1), (0, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3)])
    (True, [0, 1, 2, 3])
    >>> topo_order(3, [(0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 0)])
    (False, [0, 1, 2])
    """
